spots.name: Araku Tribal Museum
spots.description: Tribal cultural museum in Araku Valley showcasing the lifestyle, indigenous arts, crafts, and instruments of 19 regional Eastern Ghats tribes, featuring live Dhimsa dance and official ITDA/GCC forest honey and organic coffee counters.
spots.backstory: Tribal cultural museum in Araku Valley showcasing the lifestyle, indigenous arts, crafts, and instruments of 19 regional Eastern Ghats tribes, featuring live Dhimsa dance and official ITDA/GCC forest honey and organic coffee counters.
spots.rules_and_hazards: Photography inside the sacred tribal deity diorama section is prohibited. Live Dhimsa tribal dance runs every 45 minutes; tipping dancers is optional but directly supports the tribal cultural troupe.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Roadside hawkers right outside the museum gate sell plastic beads as 'tribal red coral' and synthetic eucalyptus oil. Only buy inside the gated ITDA/GCC counter.
spots.authentic_purchases: Inside the museum compound is the official Girijan Co-operative Corporation (GCC) flagship outlet. Authentic certified Araku Valley Arabica coffee powder (₹140/200g), pure multi-flora forest honey (₹160/500g), wild amla candy (₹80), soapnuts, and tribal handmade bamboo hairpins and combs.

spots.name: Chaparai Water Cascades (Dumbriguda)
spots.description: Chaparai Water Cascade, located in Alluri Sitharama Raju district of Andhra Pradesh, India, is an extraordinary natural formation characterized by a series of cascading waterfalls that descend over rocky terrain. This site serves as both a vital ecological resource and a cultural landmark, reflecting the intricate relationship between the local community and their environment.
spots.backstory: Chaparai Water Cascade, located in Alluri Sitharama Raju district of Andhra Pradesh, India, is an extraordinary natural formation characterized by a series of cascading waterfalls that descend over rocky terrain. This site serves as both a vital ecological resource and a cultural landmark, reflecting the intricate relationship between the local community and their environment.
spots.rules_and_hazards: LIFE SAFETY WARNING: The rock beds are covered in microscopic river algae and are exceptionally slippery. Over 15 serious sliding accidents occur every monsoon. Stay on shallow wading areas; never step near the deep river trench.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Ensure vendors unpack and cook fresh chicken in front of you. Some stalls reheat old chicken stuffed into blackened pre-used bamboo stalks.
spots.authentic_purchases: Hot Bamboo Chicken (₹200–₹250/stalk) cooked without oil inside green bamboo shoots over open charcoal, local roasted country corn (₹25).

spots.description: Kotappakonda (Telugu: కొటప్పకొండ) is a sacred hill and major Hindu pilgrimage site located in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, India. spots.backstory: Kotappakonda (Telugu: కొటప్పకొండ) is a sacred hill and major Hindu pilgrimage site located in Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, India. It lies about 62 km from Guntur city and 20 km from Narasaraopet. The hill is renowned for the ancient Sri Trikoteswara Swamy Temple, dedicated to Lord Shiva in the form of Trikoteswara (the Lord of the Three Peaks).
spots.rules_and_hazards: CELEBRATED TRIKUTA HILL PILGRIMAGE & KOTI LINGAMS: Consecrated atop the sacred 1,587-foot hill having three distinct peaks representing the Hindu Trinity: Brahma Shikharam, Vishnu Shikharam, and Rudra Shikharam (where Lord Trikoteswara Swamy resides). Reached via a well-engineered 4 km motorable ghat road or by climbing 703 stone steps. Famous nationwide for the stupendous annual Maha Shivaratri Prabhalu festival, where surrounding villages construct 80-to-100 foot tall electrified bamboo-and-cloth illuminated chariot towers (Prabhalu) transported on decorated tractor-trailers with thunderous folk music, drawing over 10 lakh pilgrims. The hill complex also features a Deer Park, peacock sanctuary, and a 100-acre Sanjeevani herbal garden.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Aggressive troops of monkeys along the pedestrian stone stairway; keep all prasad and plastic bags securely inside backpacks.
spots.authentic_purchases: Kotappakonda Laddu prasadam (₹20), sacred bilva leaf malas, handcrafted miniature bamboo-and-cloth Prabha replicas (₹150–₹500), country sweets.

spots.name: Guthikonda Bilam (Uthikonda Caves & Dakshina Kashi Underground Shrine)
spots.description: Guttikonda Bilam, also known as Guthikonda Bilam, is a historic cave and a hill in Piduguralla Mandal, Palnadu District of Andhra Pradesh, India. Guttikonda or Guthikonda is the name of a nearby village, while "Bilam" is the Sanskrit word for "cave".
spots.backstory: Guttikonda Bilam, also known as Guthikonda Bilam, is a historic cave and a hill in Piduguralla Mandal, Palnadu District of Andhra Pradesh, India. Guttikonda or Guthikonda is the name of a nearby village, while "Bilam" is the Sanskrit word for "cave".
spots.rules_and_hazards: SACRED UNDERGROUND LIMESTONE CAVE: Ancient natural cave system revered as 'Dakshina Kashi'. Legend holds that Maharshi Muchukunda performed intense penance here during Treta Yuga, and that the demon Kalayavana was burned to ashes here by Muchukunda's gaze upon being tricked by Lord Krishna. Palnati Brahma Naidu also held political councils here before the Battle of Palnadu. Features astonishing natural stalactites and stalagmites, an underground self-manifested Shiva Lingam perpetually washed by a cool underground spring ('Paladhara'), and a natural pond ('Gundam'). Ground is uneven, moist, and rocky; non-slip trekking footwear mandatory.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Carry powerful LED flashlights/headlamps; the interior chambers are pitch dark. Avoid entering unmapped deep crevices without local guides.
spots.authentic_purchases: Cave holy spring theertham in bottles, sacred bilva leaves, local country jaggery sweets.

spots.name: Belum Caves (Underground Limestone Passages)
spots.description: Belum Caves are a limestone cave system located in Nandyal district of Andhra Pradesh, India. Extending over 3.23 km (2.01 mi), it is the second-largest cave network in the country.
spots.backstory: Belum Caves are a limestone cave system located in Nandyal district of Andhra Pradesh, India. Extending over 3.23 km (2.01 mi), it is the second-largest cave network in the country.
spots.rules_and_hazards: LONGEST TOURIST CAVES IN THE INDIAN SUBCONTINENT: Formed by the underground Chitravati River millions of years ago. Spans 3.2 km of mapped passages (1.5 km open to tourists) with stalactite and stalagmite karst formations, the musical chamber (*Saptasvarala Guha*), and the deep underground spring (*Patalaganga* at -46m depth). Oxygen levels are lower inside; industrial air blowers operate. Asthmatic and cardiac patients should limit deep walks.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Official guides inside are free of charge; do not pay unauthorized touts outside.

spots.name: Sri Veerabhadra Temple & The Hanging Pillar of Lepakshi
spots.description: Veerabhadra temple is a Hindu temple located in the Lepakshi, in the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. The temple is dedicated to Virabhadra, a fierce form of Shiva, a major deity in Hinduism. Built in the 16th century, the architectural features of the temple are in the Vijayanagara style with profusion of carvings and paintings at almost every exposed surface of the temple.
spots.backstory: Veerabhadra temple is a Hindu temple located in the Lepakshi, in the state of Andhra Pradesh, India. The temple is dedicated to Virabhadra, a fierce form of Shiva, a major deity in Hinduism. Built in the 16th century, the architectural features of the temple are in the Vijayanagara style with profusion of carvings and paintings at almost every exposed surface of the temple.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ARCHITECTURAL WONDER OF THE WORLD: Built in 1538 AD by brothers Virupanna and Veeranna during the reign of Vijayanagara emperor Achyuta Deva Raya. THE HANGING PILLAR: Out of 70 massive carved stone pillars, one corner pillar does NOT touch the granite floor (visitors can pass a thin cloth underneath). HOUSES ASIA'S LARGEST FRESCO MURAL (24ft by 14ft painting of Veerabhadra on the ceiling). Also houses the colossal monolithic Nagalinga (7-headed serpent carved from a single boulder) and the footprint of Goddess Sita (*Sita Devi Padam*).
spots.scams_and_fakes: Beware of uncertified guides; official ASI guide services are available at the entrance with fixed tariff.

spots.backstory: The Thousand Pillar Temple or Rudreswara Swamy Temple is a historical Hindu temple located in the city of Hanamakonda, Telangana, India. It is dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu and Surya.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ARCHITECTURAL JEWEL OF TELANGANA: Built in 1163 AD by Kakatiya King Rudra Deva (Trikuta shrine dedicated to Shiva, Vishnu, and Surya). The star-shaped stone temple rests on a low 1-meter platform. Features a monumental monolithic black basalt Nandi bull carved with such extraordinary precision and mirror polish that chisel marks are imperceptible. 1,000 intricately carved stone pillars are positioned so that no pillar obstructs the direct view of the sanctum deity from any angle. Strict prohibition against touching ancient basalt carvings with oily hands; footwear strictly prohibited inside the stone compound.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Unauthorized guides loitering at the ASI entrance demanding ₹300 for unverified mythology; hire only ASI-licensed guides with official identity cards or use the official ASI QR-audio plaques.

spots.name: Bhadrakali Temple & Lake Promenade
spots.description: The temple is believed to be built in 625 CE by the King Pulakeshin II of Chalukya dynasty to commemorate his victory over Vengi region of Andhra Desham, as per the writings on the temple wall. spots.backstory: The temple is believed to be built in 625 CE by the King Pulakeshin II of Chalukya dynasty to commemorate his victory over Vengi region of Andhra Desham, as per the writings on the temple wall. Kakatiya kings later have adopted the temple and considered Goddess Bhadrakali as their kuladevata. A lake was also built by Ganapati-deva adjacent to the temple.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ANCIENT CHALUKYAN SHAKTI SHRINE: Established in 625 AD by Chalukya King Pulakeshin II. The deity is carved out of a 2.7m square natural stone rock face, depicting the Mother Goddess with 8 arms carrying weapons. Historical records indicate the legendary Koh-i-Noor diamond was originally studded in the left eye of this Bhadrakali deity before being looted by Alauddin Khilji's general Malik Kafur in 1310 AD. Steps lead directly to the water; caution during monsoons as lake embankments become slippery.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Touts outside selling fake 'Koh-i-Noor replica stones' or unlicensed motorized boat rides on unregulated parts of the lake; stick to Telangana Tourism's official boating counter.

spots.name: Warangal Fort & Kakatiya Kala Thoranam
spots.description: Kakatiya Kala Thoranam (also called Warangal Gate) is a historical arch in the Warangal district, of the Indian state of Telangana. The Warangal Fort has four ornamental gates which originally formed the gates to the ruins of the great Shiva temple which are known as Kakatiya Kala Thoranam or Warangal Gates.
spots.backstory: Kakatiya Kala Thoranam (also called Warangal Gate) is a historical arch in the Warangal district, of the Indian state of Telangana. The Warangal Fort has four ornamental gates which originally formed the gates to the ruins of the great Shiva temple which are known as Kakatiya Kala Thoranam or Warangal Gates.
spots.rules_and_hazards: UNESCO TENTATIVE LIST / ICON OF TELANGANA STATE EMBLEM: Built by Kakatiya King Ganapati Deva and completed by Queen Rudrama Devi in the 13th century. Consists of three concentric circular defensive rings: outer earthen wall (20 km circumference), inner stone wall made of massive un-mortared dressed granite blocks, and the central royal sanctum. The central archaeological compound holds hundreds of exquisitely carved lintels, friezes, ceiling panels, and the world-famous four monolithic stone Toranas. Do not climb ruined stone masonry; drone flying is banned without ASI security clearance.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Street vendors selling machine-printed nylon rugs claiming they are handloom GI-tagged Warangal dhurries; buy only with the official 'Handloom Mark' from TSCO weavers' cooperative showrooms.
spots.authentic_purchases: Warangal Dhurries (GI tagged woven flat rugs ₹500–₹3,500), brass scale models of Kakatiya Arch (₹250–₹1,500).

spots.name: Ramappa Temple (Sri Rudreshwara Swamy — UNESCO World Heritage Site)
spots.description: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple, Telangana Rudreshwara, popularly known as Ramappa Temple, is located in the village of Palampet approximately 200km north-east of Hyderabad, in the State of Telangana. It is the main Shiva temple in a walled complex built during the Kakatiyan period (1123-1323 CE) under rulers Rudradeva and Recharla Rudra.
spots.backstory: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple, Telangana Rudreshwara, popularly known as Ramappa Temple, is located in the village of Palampet approximately 200km north-east of Hyderabad, in the State of Telangana. It is the main Shiva temple in a walled complex built during the Kakatiyan period (1123-1323 CE) under rulers Rudradeva and Recharla Rudra.
spots.rules_and_hazards: UNESCO WORLD HERITAGE SITE (Inscribed 2021): Built in 1213 AD by Kakatiya General Recharla Rudra during the reign of King Ganapati Deva. The only temple in India named after its chief architect/sculptor, Ramappa. Constructed on a 6-foot star-shaped platform using sandbox technology that insulates the stone superstructure from earthquakes. The upper pyramidal tower (vimana) is built entirely with lightweight porous 'floating bricks' that float on water to minimize load. Features 12 monumental life-sized bracket figures (Madanikas) carved out of black basalt stone with mirror polish, depicting intricate dancers, huntresses, and musicians with flowing garments and delicate jewelry undercut from the stone. Footwear strictly prohibited inside the main mandapa; preserve quiet reverence.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Unauthorized locals outside attempting to sell ordinary red clay bricks claiming they are 'original floating bricks from the temple dome'; purchase only official ASI literature from the ticket counter.
spots.authentic_purchases: Miniature black stone carved dancing damsel replicas (₹400–₹1,500), local wild forest honey (₹350/bottle), bamboo lampshades.

spots.rules_and_hazards: LARGEST TRIBAL CONGREGATION IN ASIA (The Kumbh Mela of Central India): Sacred shrine commemorating tribal chieftains Sammakka and her daughter Saralamma who fought against Kakatiya taxation during a severe 12th-century drought. Unlike orthodox temples, there are no stone idols; devotees worship holy wooden platforms (Gaddelu) situated under ancient trees. spots.rules_and_hazards: UNIQUE DAKSHINA KASI OF TELANGANA: One of the three sacred Shiva lingams that define Trilinga Desa (Telangana/Andhra). Uniquely features two Shiva Lingas on a single stone pedestal (Panavattam) — one dedicated to Lord Shiva (Mukteshwara) and the other to Lord Yama (Kaleshwara). A miraculous hole in the Mukteshwara Lingam swallows countless pots of water poured during Abhishekam without ever overflowing, connecting to an underground water channel to the Triveni Sangam. spots.rules_and_hazards: THE WORLD'S LARGEST MULTI-STAGE LIFT IRRIGATION SCHEME: Modern mega-engineering feat lifting Godavari water from 100m elevation back up to the 600m Deccan plateau through underground surge pools, massive 139 MW pumps, and deep tunnels. The Medigadda (Lakshmi) Barrage spans 1,625 meters across the Godavari river with 85 hydraulic gates. Photography strictly prohibited near powerhouses and pump stations; viewpoint from designated public watch areas only.

spots.description: Pandavula Gutta (also Pandavula Guttalu or Pandavula Guhalu) is an ancient geological site and cave located near Kothapally village in Regonda mandal of Jayashankar Bhupalpally district in the Indian state of Telangana. It was designated as the only geoheritage site of Telangana.

spots.rules_and_hazards: PREHISTORIC MESOLITHIC ROCK ART SANCTUARY: First discovered in 1990, these sandstone rock shelters feature painted pictographs spanning from the Mesolithic era (10,000 BCE) through the medieval Kakatiya period. Depicts ancient wildlife (bison, antelopes, tigers), hunting scenes, geometric tribal symbols, and Kakatiya-era inscriptions and deities (Hanuman, Bhima). Involves 1.5 km of rock scrambling and stair climbing; wear gripping trekking shoes and carry at least 1 liter of drinking water.

Stone surfaces are uneven; watch for loose slabs.

spots.backstory: Kulpakji, also known as Kolanupaka Temple is a 2,000-year-old Śvetāmbara Jain temple in the village of Kolanupaka in Aler City, Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, India. The temple houses three deities: one each of Lord Rishabhanatha, Lord Neminatha, and Lord Mahavira.
spots.rules_and_hazards: OVER 2,000-YEAR-OLD JAIN PILGRIMAGE METROPOLIS: Historic center of Jainism in South India under the Rashtrakutas and Western Chalukyas. Features an astonishing 1.5-meter (5-foot) tall seated idol of Lord Mahavira carved out of a single monolithic emerald-green Jade stone (Firoza/Jade) — the largest jade deity in the world. The temple complex also enshrines magnificent 8th-century Tirthankara idols of Rishabhanatha and Neminatha. Footwear and leather items (belts, wallets) are strictly prohibited; conservative dress code enforced.

spots.name: Pembarthi Metal Crafts Village
spots.description: Pembarthi, a village in Telangana, India, is renowned for its metal craft, particularly linked to the Kakatiya dynasty's patronage of artisans known as Vishwakarmas. The craft has evolved from temple adornments to secular items, adapting to changing political and economic contexts while facing challenges such as rising material costs and youth migration.

spots.name: Bhadrachalam Sri Sita Ramachandra Swamy Temple
spots.description: The Sri Sita Ramachandraswamy Temple is a Hindu Temple dedicated to Rama, a prominent avatar of the god Vishnu. It is located on the banks of the Godavari River in the town of Bhadrachalam in east Telangana, India. Often simply referred to as Bhadrachalam or Bhadragiri, Bhadradri, the temple is considered one of the Divya Kshetrams of Godavari and is also revered as Dakshina Ayodhya.
spots.backstory: The Sri Sita Ramachandraswamy Temple is a Hindu Temple dedicated to Rama, a prominent avatar of the god Vishnu. It is located on the banks of the Godavari River in the town of Bhadrachalam in east Telangana, India. Often simply referred to as Bhadrachalam or Bhadragiri, Bhadradri, the temple is considered one of the Divya Kshetrams of Godavari and is also revered as Dakshina Ayodhya.
spots.rules_and_hazards: THE AYODHYA OF SOUTH INDIA: Established in the 17th century by the saint-devotee Kancharla Gopanna (Bhakta Ramadasu), who served as Tahsildar under Sultan Tana Shah of the Qutb Shahi Dynasty. Features the unique Vaikuntha Rama form where Lord Rama holds the Bow (Dhanus), Arrow (Bana), Conch (Shankha), and Discus (Chakra) while embracing Goddess Sita on his lap. Traditional attire (dhoti/pyjama for men, saree/salwar for women) strictly required for inner pradakshina. Footwear must be deposited at temple stands for ₹5.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Unauthorized persons selling fake 'pearls from Godavari'; real pearls are not found in the river; buy only verified gemstones with BIS hallmarking from town jewelers.
spots.authentic_purchases: Bhadrachalam Laddu prasadam (₹25), authentic Bhakta Ramadasu devotional audio recordings, pure silver Rama-Lakshmana-Sita lockets, bamboo tribal flutes.

spots.rules_and_hazards: REVERED RAMAYANA ARANYA KANDA SITE: The scenic hermitage where Lord Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana are believed to have spent their years in exile (Vanavasa). spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC 1,000-YEAR-OLD ROCK FORTRESS: Initiated in 950 AD by Kakatiya rulers and significantly expanded by the Musunuri Nayaks, Velama chiefs, Bahmanis, and Qutb Shahis. Requires climbing 150 stone steps; handrails provided on main flight. Caution near open ramparts without parapet walls.

spots.description: Nirmal district in Telangana was once famous as a production centre of as diverse things as cannons and toys. spots.backstory: Nirmal district in Telangana was once famous as a production centre of as diverse things as cannons and toys. While the foundry supplied heavy artillery to the army of the Nizam of Hyderabad, the Naqqash craftsmen and artists brought out exquisite wooden toys and duco paintings under the name of Nirmal Art.
spots.rules_and_hazards: CELEBRATED 400-YEAR-OLD CRAFT HERITAGE (GI Tagged): Founded in the 16th century under the patronage of local chieftains (Nimma Naidu). Artisans belong to the 'Naqqash' community who use locally harvested soft, lightweight 'Ponki Chekka' (Wrightia tinctoria wood) and natural mineral/vegetable colors sealed with herbal lac glaze. Visitors are welcome inside the cooperative workshops to watch the master craftsmen.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Cheap plastic and MDF board replicas sold at highway bypass shops; look for the GI certification and buy directly from the Nirmal Toy Artisans Industrial Cooperative Society (Nirmal Toys Craft Centre).
spots.authentic_purchases: GI TAGGED NIRMAL TOYS & ART: Handcrafted wooden fruit baskets (₹350–₹1,200), animal and bird figures, lacquerware trays, traditional Nirmal gold-finish paintings on wood depicting Ajanta and Kangra styles (₹800–₹6,500).

spots.name: Jodeghat Kumuram Bheem Martyr's Memorial & Tribal Museum
spots.description: The museum stands out as one of the most historically significant locations in terms of Asifabad's tribal culture and Heritage. On September 1, 1940, Adivasi fighter Kumuram Bheem and his companions were martyred at Jodeghat, and the location developed a reputation for bravery and courage.
spots.backstory: The museum stands out as one of the most historically significant locations in terms of Asifabad's tribal culture and Heritage. On September 1, 1940, Adivasi fighter Kumuram Bheem and his companions were martyred at Jodeghat, and the location developed a reputation for bravery and courage.
spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC CRADLE OF THE GOND REVOLUTION: The sacred forest sanctuary where legendary Adivasi tribal leader Kumuram Bheem fought and achieved martyrdom on 1 September 1940 resisting the Nizam's armed forces. He coined the immortal slogan 'Jal, Jangal, Zameen' (Water, Forest, Land). The state memorial complex features an impressive statue, the martyrs' memorial stupa, and a rich tribal ethnography museum exhibiting Gond, Kolam, Thotti, and Pardhan tribal artifacts, musical horns (Tudum), and hunting weapons.
spots.scams_and_fakes: None. Respect tribal sanctums and do not film sacred tribal rituals without elder permission.
spots.authentic_purchases: Authentic Gond Dokra brass artifacts (₹400–₹2,500), wild forest honey (₹350/bottle), Gondi embroidered shawls.

spots.backstory: Dichpally Ramalayam is a Lord Rama temple located in Dichpally Village of Nizamabad, Telangana built in 14th century by Kakatiya kings. As the temple has a lot of resemblance in its style and structure, it is also called the Indhoor Khajuraho or the Khajuraho of Nizamabad.
spots.rules_and_hazards: CELEBRATED 14TH-CENTURY STONE MASTERPIECE: Built by the Kakatiya rulers out of finely dressed white and black basalt stone. Highly renowned for its exquisite erotic sculptures, celestial dancers (Apsaras), musicians, and mythical Makaras carved on temple exterior walls, earning it the title 'Khajuraho of Telangana'. Incomplete without a vimana tower, giving the upper structure an enigmatic open terrace design. Climbing on ancient carved stone railings is strictly forbidden.

spots.description: Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple (Telugu: కొండగట్టు ఆంజనేయస్వామి ఆలయం) is a prominent Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman (Anjaneya), situated on a hill near Muthyumpeta village in Mallial mandal of Jagitial district, Telangana, India.
spots.backstory: Kondagattu Anjaneya Swamy Temple (Telugu: కొండగట్టు ఆంజనేయస్వామి ఆలయం) is a prominent Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Hanuman (Anjaneya), situated on a hill near Muthyumpeta village in Mallial mandal of Jagitial district, Telangana, India.
spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC 400-YEAR-OLD SANJEEVI HILL SHRINE: Built by cowherd Singam Sanjeevudu in the 17th century. The deity of Sri Sanjeeva Anjaneya is uniquely carved out of a natural rock face with two faces (Narasimha and Hanuman) and four arms holding the conch, discus, mace, and Sanjeevani hill. Renowned across Telangana for the 40-day Hanuman Deeksha vows and for curing mental ailments. 150 stone steps lead from the lower parking; modern ghat road also available. Beware of aggressive troops of monkeys; keep bags sealed.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Unauthorized vendors selling fake brass yantras along the hill path; buy genuine Devasthanam prasad and puja articles at official computerized counters.

spots.backstory: Jagtial Fort (also Jagityal Fort) is a historic star-shaped fort located in Jagtial town, Jagitial District, Telangana, approximately 190 km from Hyderabad. The fort is officially described by the Jagtial district administration as the only star-shaped fort in Telangana and is surrounded by a water-filled moat.
spots.rules_and_hazards: RARE 17TH-CENTURY EUROPEAN STAR FORTRESS: Built in the mid-17th century under the regional Nawab Ibrahim Dhamsa with engineering design by French military engineers (Jack & Tal, after whom the town is traditionally named). Features a classical star-shaped geometric ground plan surrounded by a deep double-walled defensive water moat, wooden drawbridges, rampart bastions with cannon ports, and underground ammunition vaults. Do not lean over unbarricaded moat ledges.

spots.backstory: Sri Raja Rajeshwara Temple is one of the most famous Hindu temples in Telangana, India, dedicated to Lord Shiva. It is located in the town of Vemulawada, Telangana, India. Historically the region was the capital of the Vemulawada Chalukyas who ruled from 750 to 973 CE.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ONE OF TELANGANA'S MOST SACRED SHAIVITE SHRINES (Dakshina Kasi): Built by the Vemulawada Chalukyas in the 8th century CE under King Bhadradeva. Revered for the unique 'Kode Mokku' ritual where devotees tie a holy calf and perform pradakshina around the sanctum for the fulfillment of prayers. Features the sacred Dharma Gundam (a natural stone temple pond) believed to possess curative mineral properties. Also houses a historic Dargah inside the temple courtyard, standing as a living symbol of religious harmony. Traditional attire mandatory; take ritual bath in the pond only inside designated cordoned zones.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Touts at the temple entrance demanding ₹500 for 'Kode Mokku cow rental'; perform the ritual only through the official Devasthanam counter which provides vetted sacred calves for the circumambulation.

spots.backstory: Siricilla (also spelled as Sircilla or Sirsilla) is a town and the district headquarters of Rajanna Siricilla district in the Indian state of Telangana. It is located on the banks of Manair river in the Siricilla mandal of Siricilla revenue division. It is popularly known as Textile Town due to the presence of large number of power looms, textile processing and dyeing units.
spots.rules_and_hazards: TEXTILE CITY OF TELANGANA: Sircilla is the historic powerhouse of Telangana's textile industry, operating over 35,000 power looms and centuries-old handloom guilds. Renowned globally for master weaver Nalla Vijay, who gained international fame for hand-weaving a saree that fits inside a matchbox and another that passes through a finger ring. Visitors can tour the Textile Park, view pit looms, and purchase directly from cooperative societies.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Synthetic mill-made fabric passed off as handloom silk; buy only from certified TSCO government outlets or registered Sircilla Weavers' Industrial Cooperative Societies with the 'Silk Mark'.

spots.description: Elgandal Fort is situated amidst palm groves on the banks of the Manair River (a tributary of the Godavari River), approximately 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from Karimnagar on the Sircilla Road in the Indian state of Telangana.

spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC CITADEL OF FIVE DYNASTIES: Built originally by the Kakatiyas in the 11th century, and subsequently held by the Musunuri Nayaks, Bahmanis, Qutb Shahis, Mughals, and Asaf Jahis. Perched atop a sheer granite hill surrounded by a deep defensive moat. Features imposing stone gateways, Alamgir Mosque with swaying minarets, ammunition magazines, the historic Sri Narasimha Swamy temple, and natural stepwells. 300 stone steps lead to the upper citadel; carry water; no railings on outer cliff ramparts.

spots.rules_and_hazards: WORLD-FAMOUS GEOGRAPHICAL INDICATION (GI) SILVER ART: Practiced for over 200 years in Karimnagar. spots.name: Chaya Someswara Temple (Optical Physics Shadow Mystery)
spots.description: Chaya Someshwara Temple is a Shaivite Hindu temple located in Panagal, Nalgonda district of Telangana, India. It was built around the mid-11th century during the rule of the Kunduru Chodas (a branch of Telugu Cholas), supported and embellished further by later Hindu dynasties of Telangana. Some date it to late 11th to early 12th-century.
spots.backstory: Chaya Someshwara Temple is a Shaivite Hindu temple located in Panagal, Nalgonda district of Telangana, India. It was built around the mid-11th century during the rule of the Kunduru Chodas (a branch of Telugu Cholas), supported and embellished further by later Hindu dynasties of Telangana. Some date it to late 11th to early 12th-century.
spots.rules_and_hazards: PHYSICS AND ARCHITECTURAL MARVEL: 11th-century temple built by the Kunduru Chola kings. Inside the sanctum, a distinct, dark, stationary shadow of a pillar falls continuously across the front of the Shivalinga 24 hours a day, from sunrise to sunset. However, there is NO pillar standing opposite to cast such a shadow. The phenomenon is an astonishing optical physics demonstration of multiple light refraction and slit reflection engineered into the pillared hall.

spots.name: Yadadri Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Mahakshetram
spots.description: The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple or Yadadri or Yadagiri Gutta Devasthanam (YGD), or Pancha Narasimha Kshetram or Rishi Aradhana Kshetram is a Hindu Temple situated on a hillock in the small town of Yadagirigutta in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of the Indian state of Telangana.
spots.backstory: The Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Swamy Temple or Yadadri or Yadagiri Gutta Devasthanam (YGD), or Pancha Narasimha Kshetram or Rishi Aradhana Kshetram is a Hindu Temple situated on a hillock in the small town of Yadagirigutta in the Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district of the Indian state of Telangana.
spots.rules_and_hazards: MODERN ARCHITECTURAL WONDER OF INDIA: Entirely reconstructed out of 2.5 lakh tonnes of monolithic black stone (Krishna Shila) without using a single kilogram of cement or steel, adhering strictly to the ancient Pancharatra Agama Shastras. Enshrines the ancient natural cave sanctum where Lord Narasimha appeared in five manifestations (Jwala, Yogananda, Gandabherunda, Ugra, and Lakshmi Narasimha). Features colossal carved Prahlada Charitra stone columns and grand 7-tiered Rajagopurams. Strict dress code: traditional Indian attire; mobile phones and electronic devices strictly deposited at automated lockers.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Unauthorized persons offering 'direct VIP sanctum entry' for cash; purchase all darshan tickets only at the official computerized Devasthanam counters.
spots.authentic_purchases: Yadadri pure ghee Laddu prasadam (₹35), consecrated silver Narasimha lockets, brass puja items, traditional cotton dhotis.
spots.fees: General Darshan: Free. Special Darshan: ₹150. VIP Break Darshan: ₹300. Ghat Road Toll: ₹50.

spots.name: Bhongir Fort (Bhuvanagiri Monolithic Citadel)
spots.description: Bhongir Fort, also known as Bhuvanagiri Fort, is a fort located in the heart of Bhongir a town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, India. It is located on a huge rock at a commanding height. 47 km from Hyderabad.
spots.backstory: Bhongir Fort, also known as Bhuvanagiri Fort, is a fort located in the heart of Bhongir a town in Yadadri Bhuvanagiri district, Telangana, India. It is located on a huge rock at a commanding height. 47 km from Hyderabad.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ASTONISHING 10TH-CENTURY CHALUKYAN MONOLITHIC FORT: Built in 1076 CE by Western Chalukya King Tribhuvanamalla Vikramaditya VI on a single colossal, smooth egg-shaped granite rock covering 50 acres. Later reinforced by Queen Rudrama Devi and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah. Features the royal Bala Hisar citadel, an ancient cannon on the summit, underground escape tunnels, and perennial rock cisterns. Involves a steep 45-minute climb up bare granite rock; handrail cables are installed along the route; wear gripping rubber-soled shoes; avoid climbing in rain as the granite rock becomes slippery.
spots.authentic_purchases: Local country sweets, cold sugarcane juice (₹20), historical fort maps.

spots.rules_and_hazards: GLOBAL WEAVING METROPOLIS (UNWTO World Best Tourism Village): Celebrated worldwide for its unique 'Tie-and-Dye' Ikat weaving technique where warp and weft threads are precision-dyed before weaving into intricate mathematical geometric patterns. spots.name: Sarala Sagar Dam & Unique Automated Siphon Spillway
spots.description: Sarala Sagar Project is the second biggest dam in Asia with siphon technology. It is the oldest project in India after independence Raja of Wanaparthy Raja Rameshwara Rao founded by the Sarala Sagar Dam Project that has incorporated siphon technology from California, United States. 1949 project was inaugurated by the military former Governor of Hyderabad General J.N Chowdary.
spots.backstory: Sarala Sagar Project is the second biggest dam in Asia with siphon technology. It is the oldest project in India after independence Raja of Wanaparthy Raja Rameshwara Rao founded by the Sarala Sagar Dam Project that has incorporated siphon technology from California, United States. 1949 project was inaugurated by the military former Governor of Hyderabad General J.N Chowdary.
spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC HYDRAULIC ENGINEERING MARVEL (FIRST IN ASIA): Commissioned in 1959 by Raja Rameshwar Rao III, named after his mother Rani Sarala Devi. The first dam in Asia and second in the world constructed with automated Californian saddle hooded siphon technology. When water rises to full reservoir level, siphons prime automatically using atmospheric pressure to discharge flood water without any motorized or electrical gates. Fascinating study for engineers and students. Stay off the siphon crest walls.

spots.rules_and_hazards: UNESCO TENTATIVE LIST / BADAMI CHALUKYAN MASTERPIECE: Built between the 7th and 8th centuries CE by the Western Chalukyas of Badami under King Vikramaditya I. A magnificent cluster of nine sandstone temples dedicated to Lord Shiva (Bala Brahma, Kumara Brahma, Arka Brahma, Vira Brahma, Vishva Brahma, Taraka Brahma, Garuda Brahma, Svarga Brahma, and Padma Brahma). Showcases northern Rekha-Nagara curvilinear spires, intricately carved doorway dvarapalas, and ceiling rosettes. Do not touch or climb on ancient sculptures.

spots.name: Gadwal Handloom Silk Saree Weavers' Guilds
spots.description: The history of the Gadwal handloom cluster is deeply rooted in the evolution of princely patronage, caste-based weaving traditions, and sacred-cultural functions that gave rise to one of South India's most celebrated silk saree traditions.
spots.backstory: The history of the Gadwal handloom cluster is deeply rooted in the evolution of princely patronage, caste-based weaving traditions, and sacred-cultural functions that gave rise to one of South India's most celebrated silk saree traditions.
spots.rules_and_hazards: WORLD-CELEBRATED WEAVING TRADITION (GI Tagged): Famous for over 300 years. The unique hallmark of a true Gadwal saree is the 'Kuttu' interlocking weft technique, where the body of the saree is hand-woven in uncrushable pure fine cotton while the border and pallu are woven separately in pure mulberry silk and pure gold/silver zari, then smoothly interlocked by three weavers operating simultaneous shuttles. Visitors can watch master weavers work pit looms.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Factory-printed synthetic mill textiles passed off as authentic handloom Gadwal sarees; always verify the official GI Tag certification and 'Silk Mark' / 'Handloom Mark'; purchase directly from the Gadwal Handloom Weavers' Cooperative Society (GHWCS).

spots.backstory: Narayanpet district of Telangana is renowned for its exquisite and unique cotton handloom and silk sarees, which are widely popular. There is a historic legacy behind the handloom industry of Narayanpet.
spots.rules_and_hazards: PRESTIGIOUS 350-YEAR-OLD MARATHA-DECCAN WEAVING TRADITION (GI Tagged): Tracing back to 1630 CE when the traveling army of Chhatrapati Shivaji camped in this region; weaver families traveling with the royal entourage settled here under the patronage of local chieftains. Known for their distinct earthy colors (contrasting dual borders), temple chevron borders, and lightweight feel. Visitors can explore open home workshops.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Powerloom synthetic polyester sarees sold by unverified merchants claiming to be genuine handloom Narayanpet weaves; look for the GI Tag certificate and 'Handloom Mark'; purchase directly from the Narayanpet Handloom Weavers' Cooperative Society (NHWCS).
spots.authentic_purchases: WORLD-FAMOUS GI TAGGED NARAYANPET SAREES: Pure silk Narayanpet sarees with gold zari border (₹4,500–₹16,000), superfine mercerized 80s count cotton sarees with distinct temple motif double borders (₹1,200–₹3,500), handloom stoles, ethnic dress fabrics.

spots.name: Medak Cathedral (The Diocese of Medak)
spots.description: Medak Cathedral at Medak in Telangana, India, is one of the largest churches in India and has been the cathedral church of the Diocese of Medak of the Church of South India since 1947. Originally built by Charles Walker Posnett British Wesleyan Methodists, it was consecrated on 25 December 1924.
spots.backstory: Medak Cathedral at Medak in Telangana, India, is one of the largest churches in India and has been the cathedral church of the Diocese of Medak of the Church of South India since 1947. Originally built by Charles Walker Posnett British Wesleyan Methodists, it was consecrated on 25 December 1924.
spots.rules_and_hazards: ASIA'S LARGEST GOTHIC CATHEDRAL & ARCHITECTURAL MASTERPIECE: Built between 1914 and 1924 under the vision of British Methodist missionary Reverend Charles Walker Posnett. The cathedral measures 200 feet in length and 100 feet in width with an imposing 175-foot high bell tower. Can accommodate over 5,000 worshippers inside its cavernous interior. World-renowned for its three monumental stained-glass windows imported from England depicting the Nativity, the Crucifixion, and the Ascension of Christ. Strict reverence must be maintained; mobile phones on silent; photography permitted outside prayer hours.

spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC 12TH-CENTURY KAKATIYA HILL CITADEL: Built originally by Kakatiya King Prataparudra as 'Methuku Durgam' (cooked rice fort) and later fortified by the Bahmanis and Qutb Shahis. Perched atop a massive granite hill with three imposing concentric stone gateways: 'Prathama Dwaram', 'Simha Dwaram' (flanked by double-headed Ganda Bherunda eagles), and 'Gaja Dwaram'. Houses a 17th-century 10-foot bronze cannon, Mubarak Mahal palace ruins, and natural rock water tanks. Involves climbing over 500 stone steps; physically demanding; carry water.

spots.rules_and_hazards: HISTORIC 1922 MASONRY WEIR DAM: Built by the Nizam across the Allair river between 1916 and 1922. Famous for its unique masonry weir design where excess water overflows in a smooth, wide sheet without floodgates, creating a natural water slide where tourists wade. Adjacent 130 sq.km wildlife sanctuary harbors leopards, nilgai, chinkara, and over 150 species of resident and migratory waterbirds. Algae on the weir crest makes stones extremely slippery; tread cautiously.

Attracts over 20 lakh pilgrims during the annual 3-month Brahmotsavam (Sankranti to Ugadi). Courtyards are coated in yellow turmeric powder; carry socks as stone floors get hot.

spots.name: Komati Cheruvu & Glow Garden (Mini Tank Bund)
spots.description: Komati Cheruvu, popularly known as the Mini Tank Bund of Siddipet, is a prominent lake and recreational destination in Siddipet town, Siddipet district, Telangana. The lake has been developed with a range of tourism and recreation facilities, including the Ruby Necklace Suspension Bridge, gardens, boating, a Dinosaur Theme Park, a musical fountain, and a 4-km necklace road.

spots.name: Cheriyal Scroll Paintings & Mask Artisans Guild (GI Tagged)
spots.description: Cheriyal (Cherial) is a town and municipality in Siddipet district, Telangana, an hour's drive from Hyderabad and 85 km from Warangal city. Known worldwide for its unique scroll paintings and ritual masks created by the Nakashi artisans.
spots.backstory: Cheriyal (Cherial) is a town and municipality in Siddipet district, Telangana, an hour's drive from Hyderabad and 85 km from Warangal city. Known worldwide for its unique scroll paintings and ritual masks created by the Nakashi artisans.
spots.rules_and_hazards: PRESTIGIOUS 400-YEAR-OLD NAKASHI SCROLL HERITAGE (GI Tagged): Unique folk art tradition practiced by the Nakashi artisan families, traditionally used by traveling balladeers to narrate the epics. Painted on treated khadi cloth with natural pigments extracted from stones and plants. Visitors can watch master artisans paint in their traditional homes.
spots.scams_and_fakes: Machine-printed paper posters sold as authentic Cheriyal paintings; ensure hand-painted cloth texture with natural colors; purchase directly from the Cheriyal Nakashi Artists Welfare Society.
spots.authentic_purchases: GI TAGGED CHERIYAL SCROLL PAINTINGS & MASKS: Narrative mythological khadi scroll paintings (₹800–₹8,500), handmade sawdust and tamarind seed paste traditional masks (₹250–₹1,500), decorative utility keyholders and wall panels.
